rationale: The prompt ('...which channels do they belong to?') naturally requests the reactor's full channel membership, not a bounded corpus — the design's binding_note correctly reflects this: r0 (channel_members) is identified only via user_id matching the reactor, with no filter tying the reactor's own channel_id to the message's channel (C_INFRA). This is a valid, distinct route interpretation from the earlier bounded-corpus variant, consistent with the actual wording. The route (CONVERSATION_MEMBERSHIP→USER→REACTION→MESSAGE→CONVERSATION→WORKSPACE) is fully and correctly implemented in the selector: channel_members.user_id→message_reactions.user_id→message_reactions.message_id→messages.channel_id→channels.team_id, with filters pinning reaction_type=thumbsup, message_id=1706001931.000000 (Priya's root-cause message), and team_id=T01WORKSPACE — matching all six route_nodes in order. The absent resolution is well-justified: the anchor message carries zero reactions, and the workspace's only stored reaction (eyes, by U01AGENBOT9) fails both the emoji and message-identity filters, correctly excluding it. The design also anticipates a subtle false lead: Olena's message ('Nice work getting to the root cause so fast, @priya 👍') contains a thumbsup emoji glyph embedded in message text immediately after the anchor message, which could be mistaken for a reaction — this is correctly negated via the engaged_but_unreacted role (Priya/Lukas/Olena textually engaged but hold no message_reactions row). Near-miss/negative referents accurately enumerate U01AGENBOT9's actual 10 channel memberships (matching base_seed exactly) and Priya/Lukas/Olena's actual 4 memberships each (C_INFRA, C_MODEL, C_GROWTH, C_FRONTEND, matching base_seed exactly), giving well-grounded, non-hint-leaking distractors. Answer_attributes are bare table.column names (channel_members.user_id, channel_members.channel_id). Access is fully supported via documented APIs (conversations.history, reactions.get, conversations.members/users.conversations) using only visible IDs, with no unsupported capability invoked. Mechanical checks report no errors and an empty computed_matches set, consistent with the absent verdict. This is a well-constructed, semantically sound absent-mode case with a plausible open-ended deliverable and meaningful embedded-text-vs-reaction distractor.
